title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Entrywise guarantees for MLE and Rank Centrality

label: cor:general-topk
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Exact top-$K$ recovery

title: Proof
body_md:
The condition \eqref{eq:general-topk-samples} implies \eqref{eq:general-baseline}, so \Cref{thm:general-entrywise} applies.
  For either estimator $a\in\{\mathrm{MLE},\mathrm{RC}\}$ and any $i\in S_K^\star$ and $j\notin S_K^\star$, $\widehat\theta_i^{a}-\widehat\theta_j^{a} \ge \theta_i^\star-\theta_j^\star -2\|\widehat{\bm\theta}^{a}-\bm\theta^\star\|_\infty$.
  By \eqref{eq:topk-gap-definition}, $\theta_i^\star-\theta_j^\star \ge\Delta_K$.
  Combining this with \eqref{eq:general-entrywise} and \eqref{eq:general-topk-samples} proves the claim for both estimators.

label: ex:heterogeneous-comparison
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:heterogeneous-comparison}
  Consider a sampling regime in which each edge $\{i,j\}$ is sampled independently with probability $p_{ij}\in[p,q]$, where $0<p\le q\le1$, and each sampled edge receives $L$ independent comparisons.
  Since $G(n,p)$ is a subgraph of this comparison graph, standard Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi spectral concentration \citep[Lemma~6.4]{ChenFanMaWang2019} implies that $\lambda_{\mathcal{D}}\gtrsim npL$ with high probability when $np\gtrsim\log n$.
  If $npL\gtrsim\kappa^2\log n$, \Cref{thm:general-entrywise} gives
  \begin{equation}
    \max_{a\in\{\mathrm{MLE},\mathrm{RC}\}}
    \left\lVert \widehat{\bm\theta}^{a}-\bm\theta^\star\right\rVert_\infty
    \lesssim \frac{\kappa\log^{3/2}n}{\sqrt{npL}}.
    \label{eq:heterogeneous-entrywise}
  \end{equation}
  In the special case $p=q$, this recovers the familiar Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi rate up to logarithmic factors \citep{ChenFanMaWang2019}.

  \Cref{tab:heterogeneous-entrywise} compares existing guarantees when applied to this graph family, including results for broader comparison models specialized to BTL.
  Here we take $\kappa=O(1)$ and $L=\Theta(1)$, and define the sampling heterogeneity ratio $\rho:=q/p$ and $a_n:=\sqrt{\log n/(np)}$.
  For all results, we assume $np\gtrsim\log n$, which is necessary for the graph to be connected with high probability.

\par\medskip\noindent
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}
  \centering
  \captionsetup{hypcap=false}
  \captionof{table}{High-probability bounds on $\ell_\infty$ error in \Cref{ex:heterogeneous-comparison}.
  All rows assume $np\gtrsim\log n$.}
  \label{tab:heterogeneous-entrywise}
  \small
  \setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
  \renewcommand{1.3}{1.3}
  \begin{tabular*}{\linewidth}{@{\extracolsep{\fill}}llll@{}}
    \toprule
    Result & Estimator & Error bound & Sampling conditions \\
    \midrule
    \citet{LiShrotriyaRinaldo2022}, Thm.~1
      & Regularized MLE & $\dfrac{\rho}{p\sqrt n}+\sqrt{\rho}\,a_n$
      & $np^2\gtrsim\rho^2$, $np\gtrsim\rho\log n$ \\[2pt]
    \citet{HanXuChen2023}
      & MLE & $\rho\,a_n\log n$
      & $np\gg\rho^2\log^3 n$ \\

      & MLE & $a_n$
      & $np\gtrsim\rho^4\log^2 n$ \\
    \citet{YangChenOrecchiaMa2024}, Thm.~1
      & SDP-weighted MLE & $a_n$
      & $np\gtrsim\log^3 n$ \\
    \citet{FanLouWangYu2026}, Thm.~4.2
      & RC & $a_n$
      & $\rho=O(1)$, $np\gg\sqrt{n\log n}$ \\

      & $\rho=O(1)$ \\

      & $np\gtrsim(n\log n)^{1/3}$ \\

      & MLE & $a_n+\dfrac{1}{p\sqrt n}$
      & $np\gtrsim\sqrt n\,\log^3 n$ \\[2pt]

\par\medskip

Our bound provides optimal error guarantees up to logarithmic factors for both MLE and Rank Centrality, with no additional assumptions.
In comparison, other existing work requires factors of $\rho=q/p$ in the error bounds \citep{LiShrotriyaRinaldo2022,HanXuChen2023} and sampling conditions \citep{LiShrotriyaRinaldo2022,HanXuChen2023,YangChenOrecchiaMa2024}, gives suboptimal error guarantees in sparse regimes \citep{LeeMakurSingh2026,LiXu2026}, or requires denser sampling regimes \citep{LiShrotriyaRinaldo2022,FanLouWangYu2026,LiXu2026}.
Moreover, it does not require the reweighting used in \citet{YangChenOrecchiaMa2024} and \citet{LeeMakurSingh2026}.

name: Heterogeneous random comparison graph

label: eq:proof-overview-contraction
title: Proof idea
body_md:
For the MLE, let $\bm\delta=\widehat{\bm\theta}^{\mathrm{MLE}}-\bm\theta^\star$, let $m$ be a median of its coordinates, and write $S_+(t)=\{i:\delta_i>m+t\}$ for $t\ge0$.
Our main technical step shows that, with high probability, for every $t\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
  \left\lvert S_+(t+a)\right\rvert\le\frac14\left\lvert S_+(t)\right\rvert,
  \qquad
  a=A\kappa\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{\lambda_{\mathcal{D}}}},
  \label{eq:proof-overview-contraction}
\end{equation}
where $A$ is a sufficiently large universal constant.
Each threshold increase by $a$ removes at least three quarters of the remaining coordinates.
Since $\left\lvert S_+(0)\right\rvert\le n/2$, the set is empty after $O(\log n)$ steps.
The largest coordinate of $\bm\delta$ therefore lies at most $O(a\log n)$ above the median.
Repeating the argument below the median and using the centering constraint gives the entrywise rate $\kappa\log^{3/2}n/\sqrt{\lambda_{\mathcal{D}}}$.

Rank Centrality follows the same principle, except that the level set and the contraction bound \eqref{eq:proof-overview-contraction} take a different form.
The shared tools and full proofs appear in \Cref{sec:shared-tools,sec:mle-proof,sec:rc-proof}.

label: lem:localized-process
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Localized edge-noise process

label: eq:fixed-vector-tail
title: Proof
body_md:
For a fixed $\bm v$, independence and \eqref{eq:edge-mgf} give
  \[
    \mathbb{E}\exp(t\bm z^\top\bm v) \le \exp\!
    \left(\frac{\tau^2t^2}{2}
    \sum_{e\in E}
    L_e\cdot(\bm b_e^\top\bm v)^2\right) =\exp\!
    \left(\frac{\tau^2t^2}{2}
    \bm v^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm v\right).
  \]
  Consequently, applying the Chernoff bound separately to $\bm z^\top\bm v$ and $-\bm z^\top\bm v$ gives
  \begin{equation}
    \mathbb{P}\!\left\{
    \left\lvert \bm z^\top\bm v\right\rvert>
    u\tau\sqrt{\bm v^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm v}
    \right\}
    \le2\exp(-u^2/2).
    \label{eq:fixed-vector-tail}
  \end{equation}

  Fix $S\subsetneq[n]$ and define
  \[
    \left\lVert \bm v\right\rVert_{\mathcal{D}} :=(\bm v^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm v)^{1/2}, \qquad \mathcal{V}_S:=\{\bm v:\operatorname{supp}(\bm v)\subseteq S\}.
  \]
  Connectedness implies that the only null vectors of $\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}$ are multiples of $\bm{1}_n$.
  Hence $\left\lVert \cdot\right\rVert_{\mathcal{D}}$ is a norm on the $s$-dimensional space $\mathcal{V}_S$.
  By a standard volumetric covering argument, its unit sphere admits a $1/2$-net $\mathcal N_S$ in this norm with $|\mathcal N_S|\le5^s$.

  Set
  \[
    M_S:=\sup_{\substack{\bm v\in\mathcal{V}_S\\\left\lVert \bm v\right\rVert_{\mathcal{D}}=1}} \left\lvert \bm z^\top\bm v\right\rvert.
  \]
  For every unit vector $\bm v$, choose $\bm q\in\mathcal N_S$ with $\left\lVert \bm v-\bm q\right\rVert_{\mathcal{D}}\le1/2$.
  The triangle inequality and the definition of $M_S$ then give
  \[
    \left\lvert \bm z^\top\bm v\right\rvert \le \left\lvert \bm z^\top(\bm v-\bm q)\right\rvert + \left\lvert \bm z^\top\bm q\right\rvert \le \frac12M_S + \left\lvert \bm z^\top\bm q\right\rvert.
  \]
  Taking the supremum over $\bm v$ and rearranging yields
  \[
    M_S = \sup_{\substack{\bm v\in\mathcal{V}_S\\\left\lVert \bm v\right\rVert_{\mathcal{D}}=1}}
    \left\lvert \bm z^\top\bm v\right\rvert
    \le2\max_{\bm q\in\mathcal N_S}\left\lvert \bm z^\top\bm q\right\rvert.
  \]
  Consequently, for every $u>0$,
  \[
    \{M_S>2u\tau\}
    \subseteq
    \bigcup_{\bm q\in\mathcal N_S}
    \left\{\left\lvert \bm z^\top\bm q\right\rvert>u\tau\right\}.
  \]
  Apply \eqref{eq:fixed-vector-tail} to the net $\mathcal N_S$ and take a union bound over the at most $\binom ns\le n^s$ supports of size $s$.
  With $u=A\sqrt{s\log n}$, the probability that $M_S>2u\tau$ for at least one support of size at most $n/2$ is bounded by
  \[
    2\sum_{s=1}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor} \binom ns\cdot 5^s\cdot\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}A^2s\log n\right) \le 2\sum_{s=1}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor} \exp\!
    \left\{s\log(5n)-\frac{1}{2}
    A^2s\log n\right\} \le Cn^{-10}
  \]
  for a sufficiently large universal constant $A$.
  On the complementary event, $M_S\le2A\tau\sqrt{s\log n}$.
  Hence, for every nonzero $\bm v\in\mathcal{V}_S$,
  \[
    \left\lvert \bm z^\top\bm v\right\rvert =\left\lVert \bm v\right\rVert_{\mathcal{D}} \left\lvert \bm z^\top\frac{\bm v}{\left\lVert \bm v\right\rVert_{\mathcal{D}}}\right\rvert \le2A\tau\sqrt{s\log n}\,\left\lVert \bm v\right\rVert_{\mathcal{D}},
  \]
  which proves \eqref{eq:localized-process} after absorbing $2A$ into $C$.

label: lem:sparse-poincare
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Sparse-support Poincar\'e inequality

label: eq:sparse-poincare-variational
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\overline v=n^{-1}\bm{1}_n^\top\bm v$.
  Since $\bm v-\overline v\bm{1}_n\perp\bm{1}_n$, the standard variational characterization of $\lambda_{\mathcal{D}}=\lambda_2(\bm L_{\mathcal{D}})$ gives
  \begin{equation}
    \bm v^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm v
    =(\bm v-\overline v\bm{1}_n)^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}
    (\bm v-\overline v\bm{1}_n)
    \ge\lambda_{\mathcal{D}}\left\lVert \bm v-\overline v\bm{1}_n\right\rVert_2^2.
    \label{eq:sparse-poincare-variational}
  \end{equation}
  If $S=\operatorname{supp}(\bm v)$ and $|S|\le n/2$, then Cauchy--Schwarz gives
  \[
    n\overline v^2 =\frac{(\sum_{i\in S}v_i)^2}{n} \le\frac{|S|}{n}\left\lVert \bm v\right\rVert_2^2 \le\frac12\left\lVert \bm v\right\rVert_2^2.
  \]
  Consequently, $\left\lVert \bm v-\overline v\bm{1}_n\right\rVert_2^2=\left\lVert \bm v\right\rVert_2^2-n\overline v^2 \ge\left\lVert \bm v\right\rVert_2^2/2$.
  Combining this with \eqref{eq:sparse-poincare-variational} finishes the proof.

label: lem:spectral-cut-size
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Cut weight from algebraic connectivity

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\bm x=\bm{1}_S-(|S|/n)\bm{1}_n$.
  Then $\bm x\perp\bm{1}_n$, $\bm x^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm x=\sum_{e\in\partial S}L_e$, and $\left\lVert \bm x\right\rVert_2^2=|S|(n-|S|)/n$.
  The variational definition of $\lambda_{\mathcal{D}}$ proves the claim.

label: lem:mle-existence
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Strong connectivity implies a finite unique MLE

label: eq:ordered-win-loss
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $N_{ij}$ be the number of observed wins of item $i$ over item $j$.
  Equivalently, grouping the terms in \eqref{eq:mle-loss} by their observed winner gives
  \begin{equation}
    \mathcal{L}(\bm\theta)
    =\sum_{i\ne j}
    N_{ij} \log\!
    \left(1+\mathrm{e}^{\theta_j-\theta_i}\right).
    \label{eq:ordered-win-loss}
  \end{equation}
  Its Hessian is
  \[
    \nabla^2\mathcal{L}(\bm\theta) =\sum_{e\in E}L_e\cdot\sigma'(\bm b_e^\top\bm\theta) \bm b_e\bm b_e^\top.
  \]
  Every coefficient is positive.
  Since the comparison graph $G$ is connected, the Hessian's nullspace is $\operatorname{span}\{\bm{1}_n\}$ and the loss is strictly convex on $\mathcal{H}$.

  For coercivity, take any sequence $\bm\theta^{(m)}\in\mathcal{H}$ with $\left\lVert \bm\theta^{(m)}\right\rVert_2\to\infty$.
  Its coordinate range $R_m=\max_i\theta_i^{(m)}-\min_i\theta_i^{(m)}$ tends to infinity.
  Among the ordered coordinates, some consecutive gap is at least $R_m/(n-1)$.
  Let $S_m$ and $[n]\setminus S_m$ be the sets of items separated by this gap, with $\theta_i^{(m)}<\theta_j^{(m)}$ for all $i\in S_m$ and $j\in[n]\setminus S_m$.
  Strong connectivity supplies a directed edge $j\to i$ of $D_{\mathrm{win}}$ with $i\in S_m$ and $j\notin S_m$.
  Thus item $i$ defeats item $j$ at least once.
  Its contribution to \eqref{eq:ordered-win-loss} is at least
  \[
    \log\!
    \left(1+\mathrm{e}^{\theta_j^{(m)}-\theta_i^{(m)}}\right)
    \ge\frac{R_m}{n-1}.
  \]
  Thus the loss is at least as large as this term and is coercive because $R_m\to\infty$.
  Continuity, coercivity, and strict convexity of $\mathcal{L}$ on $\mathcal{H}$ yield a unique minimizer.

label: lem:mle-score-localization
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: MLE score identity and localized score control

title: Proof
body_md:
At a constrained minimizer on $\mathcal{H}$, the gradient is orthogonal to $\mathcal{H}$ and therefore belongs to $\operatorname{span}\{\bm{1}_n\}$.
  On the other hand, $\nabla\mathcal{L}(\bm\theta)\perp\bm{1}_n$ for every $\bm\theta$, because the loss is invariant under common shifts.
  The constrained first-order condition thus gives $\nabla\mathcal{L}(\widehat{\bm\theta}^{\mathrm{MLE}})=0$.
  Subtracting $\nabla\mathcal{L}(\bm\theta^\star)=\bm g_{\mathrm{MLE}}$ and expanding the gradient difference gives \eqref{eq:mle-score-identity}.

  Condition on the observation design $\mathcal{D}$.
  The variables $\zeta_e=L_e\cdot\{\sigma(\bm b_e^\top\bm\theta^\star)-\overline Y_e\}$ are independent and centered.
  Hoeffding's lemma gives $\mathbb{E}\exp(t\zeta_e)\le\exp(L_et^2/8)$.
  Applying \Cref{lem:localized-process} with a universal $\tau$ proves \eqref{eq:mle-localized-score}.
head: environment

label: lem:logistic-increment
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Logistic increment lower bound

title: Proof
body_md:
For $|z|\le\log\kappa+1$,
  \[
    \sigma'(z)=\frac1{\mathrm{e}^{-z}+2+\mathrm{e}^z}\ge\frac1{2(\mathrm{e}+1)\kappa}.
  \]
  If $|u|\le1$, the mean value theorem therefore gives
  \[
    |\sigma(x+u)-\sigma(x)|\ge \frac{1}{2(\mathrm{e}+1)\kappa}|u|.
  \]
  If $u>1$, monotonicity of $\sigma$ gives
  \[
    |\sigma(x+u)-\sigma(x)|\ge |\sigma(x+1)-\sigma(x)| \ge \frac{1}{2(\mathrm{e}+1)\kappa}.
  \]
  If $u<-1$, the analogous comparison in the opposite direction gives
  \[
    |\sigma(x+u)-\sigma(x)|\ge |\sigma(x-1)-\sigma(x)| \ge \frac{1}{2(\mathrm{e}+1)\kappa}.
  \]
  This proves the first inequality in \eqref{eq:logistic-increment}, and the second follows from $\mathrm{e}<3$.
head: environment

label: lem:mle-truncated-energy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:mle-truncated-energy}
  Assume that \eqref{eq:mle-localized-score} in \Cref{lem:mle-score-localization} holds.
  Fix $t\in\mathbb{R}$ and $a\in(0,1]$, and define $\bm v$ by
  \[
    v_i:=T_{t,a}(\delta_i), \qquad i\in[n].
  \]
  Let $S:=\{i:\delta_i>t\}$.
  If $1\le |S|\le n/2$, then
  \begin{align}
    \bm v^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm v
     & \le C\kappa^2|S|\log n,
    \label{eq:mle-energy}                            \\
    \left\lVert \bm v\right\rVert_2^2
     & \le C\frac{\kappa^2}{\lambda_{\mathcal{D}}}|S|\log n.
    \label{eq:mle-l2-truncation}
  \end{align}
  For the lower truncation, define
  \[
    \widetilde T_{t,a}(z):=-\min\{(t-z)_+,a\}, \qquad v_i:=\widetilde T_{t,a}(\delta_i),
  \]
  and let $S^-:=\{i:\delta_i<t\}$.
  If $1\le |S^-|\le n/2$, the same bounds hold with $|S|$ replaced by $|S^-|$.
head: environment
name: MLE truncated level-set energy

title: Proof
body_md:
For an oriented edge $e=(i,j)$, put $u=\bm b_e^\top\bm\delta = \delta_i-\delta_j$.
  Because $T_{t,a}$ is nondecreasing, $1$-Lipschitz, and takes values in $[0,a]\subset[0,1]$, $\bm b_e^\top\bm v=T_{t,a}(\delta_i)-T_{t,a}(\delta_j)$ has the same sign as $u$ and $|\bm b_e^\top\bm v|\le\min\{|u|,1\}$.
  Since $|\bm b_e^\top\bm\theta^\star|\le\log\kappa$, \Cref{lem:logistic-increment} gives
  \[
    \left[\sigma\bigl(\bm b_e^\top(\bm\theta^\star+\bm\delta)\bigr) -\sigma(\bm b_e^\top\bm\theta^\star)\right] \cdot(\bm b_e^\top\bm v) \ge \frac{1}{8\kappa}\min\{|u|,1\} \cdot \left\lvert \bm b_e^\top\bm v\right\rvert \ge\frac{1}{8\kappa}(\bm b_e^\top\bm v)^2.
  \]
  Taking the inner product of the score identity \eqref{eq:mle-score-identity} in \Cref{lem:mle-score-localization} with $\bm v$ and summing the preceding inequality over the edges yields
  \[
    -\bm g_{\mathrm{MLE}}^\top\bm v \ge\frac{1}{8\kappa} \sum_{e\in E}L_e\cdot(\bm b_e^\top\bm v)^2 =\frac{1}{8\kappa}\bm v^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm v.
  \]
  Combining this with the localized-score bound in \Cref{lem:mle-score-localization} gives
  \[
    \frac{1}{8\kappa}\bm v^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm v
    \le C\sqrt{|S|\log n}
    \sqrt{\bm v^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm v}.
  \]
  Rearranging this proves \eqref{eq:mle-energy}.
  Combining it with \Cref{lem:sparse-poincare} proves \eqref{eq:mle-l2-truncation}.
  The lower truncation works similarly.

label: lem:rc-noise-localization
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Rank Centrality edge-noise localization

label: eq:rc-noise-mgf
title: Proof
body_md:
The edgewise noise variables $\gamma_e$ are independent.
  For every edge $e=(i,j)$ and repetition $\ell\in[L_e]$, write
  \[
    X_e^{(\ell)}=\mathbf{1}\{j\text{ defeats }i\text{ in repetition }\ell\}, \qquad \widehat q_{ij}=L_e^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L_e}X_e^{(\ell)}.
  \]
  Hoeffding's lemma gives, for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$,
  \begin{equation}
    \mathbb{E}\!\left[\exp(t\gamma_e)\mid\mathcal{D}\right]
    \le \exp\!\left(
    \frac{t^2L_e\cdot(\bar\alpha_i^\star+\bar\alpha_j^\star)^2}{8}
    \right)
    \le \exp\!\left(\frac{t^2\kappa^2L_e}{2}\right).
    \label{eq:rc-noise-mgf}
  \end{equation}
  Applying \Cref{lem:localized-process} with $\tau=\kappa$ proves \eqref{eq:rc-localized-score}.
head: environment

label: lem:rc-upper-truncation-energy
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Upper stationary-flow truncation energy

label: eq:rc-cut-noise
title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that $\partial S$ denotes the edge boundary of $S$.
Let $\bm{1}_S\in\{0,1\}^n$ denote the indicator vector of $S$, and define
\begin{equation}
  \Gamma(S):=\bm{1}_S^\top\bm g_{\mathrm{RC}}.
  \label{eq:rc-cut-noise}
\end{equation}
Recall that $\{r_i\}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:rc-relative-stationary}.
For $h>0$, let $S_h^+=\{i:r_i>h\}$.
Orient every edge in $\partial S_h^+$ as $e=(i,j)$, where $i\in S_h^+$ and $j\notin S_h^+$, using the reverse direction of the fixed orientation when necessary.
Reversal changes the signs of both $\gamma_e$ and $\bm b_e$, so $\gamma_e\cdot\bm b_e$ is unchanged.
We may therefore use these outward orientations in \eqref{eq:rc-score}.
Since $\bm{1}_{S_h^+}^\top\bm b_e=1$ on every outward boundary edge and is zero on every nonboundary edge,
\[
  \Gamma(S_h^+)=\sum_{e\in\partial S_h^+}\gamma_e.
\]

Define
\[
  P^+(h):=\sum_{e\in\partial S_h^+} \left\{f_e\cdot(r_i-h)+f_{\bar e}\cdot(h-r_j)\right\}.
\]
Every summand is nonnegative because $r_i>h\ge r_j$ and the flows are nonnegative.
On the other hand, summing the stationary-flow identity \eqref{eq:rc-stationary-flow} over $S_h^+$ cancels every internal edge and leaves
\[
  0=\sum_{e\in\partial S_h^+} (f_e\cdot r_i-f_{\bar e}\cdot r_j) =P^+(h)+h\cdot\Gamma(S_h^+),
\]
where the second equality uses
\[
  f_e\cdot r_i-f_{\bar e}\cdot r_j =f_e\cdot(r_i-h)+f_{\bar e}\cdot(h-r_j) +h\cdot(f_e-f_{\bar e}).
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  P^+(h)=-h\cdot\Gamma(S_h^+)\ge0.
  \label{eq:rc-upper-cut}
\end{equation}

We next lower bound the integral of $P^+(h)$ by the Laplacian energy of $\bm z$.
Fix an edge $\{i,j\}\in E$.
If $r_i=r_j$, the edge never belongs to $\partial S_h^+$ and contributes zero to $\int_t^{t+a}P^+(h)\,dh$.
Otherwise, relabel its endpoints so that $x:=r_i>r_j=:y$.
The edge belongs to $\partial S_h^+$ exactly when $y\le h<x$.
Hence the relevant levels form the interval $I=[t,t+a]\cap[y,x)$, whose length is
\[
  \ell=T_{t,a}^+(x)-T_{t,a}^+(y)=|z_i-z_j|.
\]
Over these levels the edge is oriented from $i$ to $j$, so its contribution to $\int_t^{t+a}P^+(h)\,dh$ is
\[
  f_e\int_I(x-h)\,dh+f_{\bar e}\int_I(h-y)\,dh.
\]
If $\ell=0$, both integrals vanish.
Otherwise, write $I=[\alpha,\alpha+\ell]$ up to the choice of endpoints.
Since $y\le \alpha<\alpha+\ell\le x$,
\[
  \int_I(x-h)\,dh
  =\ell(x-\alpha)-\frac{\ell^2}{2}
  \ge\frac{\ell^2}{2},
  \qquad
  \int_I(h-y)\,dh
  =\ell(\alpha-y)+\frac{\ell^2}{2}
  \ge\frac{\ell^2}{2}.
\]
The edge-mass bound \eqref{eq:rc-edge-mass} therefore makes this contribution at least
\[
  \frac12(f_e+f_{\bar e})\ell^2
  \ge\frac12L_e\cdot(z_i-z_j)^2.
\]
Summing over the edges gives
\begin{equation}
  \int_t^{t+a}
  P^+(h)\,dh \ge\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}L_{ij}\cdot(z_i-z_j)^2 =\frac12\bm z^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm z.
  \label{eq:rc-upper-energy-lower}
\end{equation}

Define the scalar cut-integration transform
\begin{equation}
  \psi_{t,a}^+(x):=\int_t^{t+a}h\cdot\mathbf{1}\{x>h\}\,dh
  =t\cdot T_{t,a}^+(x)+\frac12T_{t,a}^+(x)^2
  \label{eq:rc-upper-cut-transform}
\end{equation}
and write $\bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r):=(\psi_{t,a}^+(r_i))_{i\in[n]}$ for its coordinatewise application to $\bm r$.
For each level $h$, the indicator of $S_h^+$ has coordinates $\mathbf{1}\{r_i>h\}$.
Hence \eqref{eq:rc-cut-noise} and an interchange of the finite sum with the integral give
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
    \int_t^{t+a}h\cdot\Gamma(S_h^+)\,dh
    &=\sum_{i=1}^n g_{\mathrm{RC},i}
      \int_t^{t+a}h\cdot\mathbf{1}\{r_i>h\}\,dh \\
    &=\sum_{i=1}^n g_{\mathrm{RC},i}\cdot\psi_{t,a}^+(r_i)
     =\bm g_{\mathrm{RC}}^\top\bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r).
  \end{aligned}
  \label{eq:rc-upper-cut-integration}
\end{equation}
The vector $\bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r)$ is supported on $\{r>t\}$.
Moreover, since $T_{t,a}^+(x),T_{t,a}^+(y)\in[0,a]$, the identity \eqref{eq:rc-upper-cut-transform} gives
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
    \left\lvert \psi_{t,a}^+(x)-\psi_{t,a}^+(y)\right\rvert
    &=\left\lvert T_{t,a}^+(x)-T_{t,a}^+(y)\right\rvert
      \left\{t+\frac{T_{t,a}^+(x)+T_{t,a}^+(y)}{2}\right\} \\
    &\le(t+a)\cdot\left\lvert T_{t,a}^+(x)-T_{t,a}^+(y)\right\rvert.
  \end{aligned}
  \label{eq:rc-upper-lipschitz}
\end{equation}

  Combine \eqref{eq:rc-upper-cut}, \eqref{eq:rc-upper-energy-lower}, and \eqref{eq:rc-upper-cut-integration} to obtain
  \[
    \frac12\bm z^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm z \le-\bm g_{\mathrm{RC}}^\top\bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r).
  \]
  Since $\bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r)$ is supported on $\{i:r_i>t\}$, whose size is $s$, we may apply \eqref{eq:rc-localized-score} from \Cref{lem:rc-noise-localization} with $\bm v=\bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r)$ to obtain
  \[
    -\bm g_{\mathrm{RC}}^\top\bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r)
    \le \left\lvert \bm g_{\mathrm{RC}}^\top\bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r)\right\rvert
    \le C\kappa\sqrt{s\log n}\cdot
    \sqrt{\bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r)^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}
      \bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r)}.
  \]
  Moreover, applying \eqref{eq:rc-upper-lipschitz} to every edge and using $z_i=T_{t,a}^+(r_i)$ gives
  \[
    \begin{aligned}
      \bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r)^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}
        \bm\psi_{t,a}^+(\bm r)
      &=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}L_{ij}\cdot
        \left\lvert \psi_{t,a}^+(r_i)-\psi_{t,a}^+(r_j)\right\rvert^2 \\
      &\le (t+a)^2\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}L_{ij}\cdot(z_i-z_j)^2
       =(t+a)^2\bm z^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm z.
    \end{aligned}
  \]
  Combining these two bounds with the preceding display yields
  \[
    \frac12\bm z^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm z
    \le C\kappa\sqrt{s\log n}
    (t+a)\cdot\sqrt{\bm z^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm z}.
  \]
  Rearranging this gives \eqref{eq:rc-upper-truncation-energy} and completes the proof.

label: lem:rc-lower-truncation-energy
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Lower stationary-flow truncation energy

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $\widetilde{\bm r}:=-\bm r$.
  The stationary-flow identity \eqref{eq:rc-stationary-flow} is linear in $\bm r$, so it also holds with $\bm r$ replaced by $\widetilde{\bm r}$.
  Apply the upper-cut argument from the proof of \Cref{lem:rc-upper-truncation-energy} to $\widetilde{\bm r}$ over the level interval $[-t,-t+a]$.
  The upper level set at the initial level and the resulting truncation are
  \[
    \{i:\widetilde r_i>-t\}=\{i:r_i<t\},
    \qquad
    T_{-t,a}^+(\widetilde r_i)=T_{t,a}^-(r_i)=z_i.
  \]
  Thus the localized-score bound applies with support size $s$.

  It remains only to identify the Lipschitz factor in the sign-reversed argument.
  Define
  \[
    \widetilde\psi(x):=\int_{-t}^{-t+a}
      h\cdot\mathbf{1}\{x>h\}\,dh.
  \]
  Since $T_{-t,a}^+(x),T_{-t,a}^+(y)\in[0,a]$, the same factorization as in \eqref{eq:rc-upper-lipschitz} gives
  \[
    \begin{aligned}
      \left\lvert \widetilde\psi(x)-\widetilde\psi(y)\right\rvert
      &=
      \left\lvert T_{-t,a}^+(x)-T_{-t,a}^+(y)\right\rvert\cdot
      \left\lvert -t+\frac{T_{-t,a}^+(x)+T_{-t,a}^+(y)}{2}\right\rvert \\
      &\le
      t\cdot\left\lvert T_{-t,a}^+(x)-T_{-t,a}^+(y)\right\rvert.
    \end{aligned}
  \]
  The last inequality uses $a<t$.
  The remainder of the proof of \Cref{lem:rc-upper-truncation-energy}, with this Lipschitz factor, yields \eqref{eq:rc-lower-truncation-energy}.

label: lem:er-gap
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Algebraic connectivity of an Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graph

title: Proof
body_md:
The first claim follows from \citet[Lemma~6.4]{ChenFanMaWang2019}.
  If $\mathcal{D}$ contains at least $L$ observations on every edge of $G_0$, then, for every $\bm v\perp\bm{1}_n$,
  \[
    \bm v^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm v
    \ge L\bm v^\top\bm L_{G_0}\bm v.
  \]
  Taking the minimum over unit vectors orthogonal to $\bm{1}_n$ gives
  \[
    \lambda_{\mathcal{D}}
    \ge L\lambda_2(\bm L_{G_0})
    \ge\frac12npL.
  \]

label: lem:adaptive-split-localization
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Two-stage localized score control

label: eq:adaptive-initial-localization
title: Proof
body_md:
Because $G_0$ is connected and all initial edge counts are positive, $\mathcal{D}_0$ is connected.
Fix an orientation for every pair.
For $a\in\{\mathrm{MLE},\mathrm{RC}\}$, decompose the final score as
\[
  \bm g_a=\bm g_{a,0}+\bm g_{a,+},
  \qquad \tau_{\mathrm{MLE}}=1,\qquad \tau_{\mathrm{RC}}=\kappa,
\]
where the two terms contain the initial and fresh score contributions, respectively.
With $\mathcal{D}_0$ fixed, the initial edge contributions are independent and centered.
Hoeffding's lemma and \Cref{lem:localized-process}, applied to $\mathcal{D}_0$, give, except with probability $Cn^{-10}$, simultaneously for every $\bm v$ supported on a set of size $s\le n/2$,
\begin{equation}
  \left\lvert \bm g_{a,0}^\top\bm v\right\rvert
  \le C\tau_a\sqrt{s\log n}
  \sqrt{\bm v^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}_0}\bm v}.
  \label{eq:adaptive-initial-localization}
\end{equation}
This bound holds over all such test vectors, so it remains usable after the augmentation is chosen.

Let $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{aug}}$ be the sigma-field generated by $\mathcal{D}_0$, the initial outcomes, and the chosen counts $\{M_{ij}\}$.
Conditional on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{aug}}$, the fresh score contributions are independent and centered.
The same Hoeffding bounds as in the MLE and Rank Centrality proofs apply with counts $M_{ij}\le L_{ij}$.
Applying \Cref{lem:localized-process} conditionally to the connected final design $\mathcal{D}$ therefore gives, except with conditional probability $Cn^{-10}$,
\begin{equation}
  \left\lvert \bm g_{a,+}^\top\bm v\right\rvert
  \le C\tau_a\sqrt{s\log n}
  \sqrt{\bm v^\top\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}\bm v}
  \label{eq:adaptive-fresh-localization}
\end{equation}
simultaneously over the same class of test vectors.
The augmentation graph itself need not be connected.

Since $\bm L_{\mathcal{D}_0}\preceq\bm L_{\mathcal{D}}$, adding the two bounds proves \eqref{eq:adaptive-mle-localization} and \eqref{eq:adaptive-rc-localization}.
Taking a union bound over the two stages and two estimators gives probability at least $1-Cn^{-10}$.

label: prop:heterogeneous-is-semirandom
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:heterogeneous-is-semirandom}
  Fix $p\in(0,1]$ and an integer $L\ge1$.
  Suppose each pair $\{i,j\}$ is observed independently with probability $p_{ij}\in[p,1]$.
  On each observed pair, generate $L$ independent BTL comparisons.
  Then the joint law of the observed design and comparison outcomes can be realized under \Cref{def:semirandom} after drawing $G_0\sim G(n,p)$ and assigning $L$ initial comparisons to each edge of $G_0$.
head: environment
name: Heterogeneous sampling is semirandom

title: Proof
body_md:
Independently for each pair $\{i,j\}$, draw $U_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$ and set
  \[
    B_{ij}=\mathbf{1}\{U_{ij}\le p\},
    \qquad
    A_{ij}=\mathbf{1}\{U_{ij}\le p_{ij}\}.
  \]
  Since $p_{ij}\ge p$, the variables $B_{ij}$ form an initial $G(n,p)$ graph contained in the heterogeneous graph defined by the $A_{ij}$.
  Generate $L$ initial comparisons on its edges and set
  \[
    M_{ij}=L(A_{ij}-B_{ij}).
  \]
  Since $B_{ij}\le A_{ij}$, we have $M_{ij}\ge0$, and the final count on each pair is $LA_{ij}$.
  Generating the $M_{ij}$ additional comparisons in the augmentation stage gives the heterogeneous-sampling law.
